A fixed list of bend points for the edge. This is used by the 'Fixed Layout' algorithm to specify a pre-defined routing for an edge. The vector chain must include the source point, any bend points, and the target point, so it must have at least two points.

What kind of edge routing style should be applied for the content of a parent node. Algorithms may also set this option to single edges in order to mark them as splines. The bend point list of edges with this option set to SPLINES must be interpreted as control points for a piecewise cubic spline.

Turns topdown layout on and off. If this option is enabled, hierarchical layout will be computed first for the root node and then for its children recursively. Layouts are then scaled down to fit the area provided by their parents. Graphs must follow a certain structure for topdown layout to work properly. {@link TopdownNodeTypes.PARALLEL_NODE} nodes must have children of type {@link TopdownNodeTypes.HIERARCHICAL_NODE} and must define {@link topdown.hierarchicalNodeWidth} and {@link topdown.hierarchicalNodeAspectRatio} for their children. Furthermore they need to be laid out using an algorithm that is a {@link TopdownLayoutProvider}. Hierarchical nodes can also be parents of other hierarchical nodes and can optionally use a {@link TopdownSizeApproximator} to dynamically set sizes during topdown layout. In this case {@link topdown.hierarchicalNodeWidth} and {@link topdown.hierarchicalNodeAspectRatio} should be set on the node itself rather than the parent. The values are then used by the size approximator as base values. Hierarchical nodes require the layout option {@link nodeSize.fixedGraphSize} to be true to prevent the algorithm used there from resizing the hierarchical node. This option is not supported if 'Hierarchy Handling' is set to 'INCLUDE_CHILDREN'

Factor for computation of animation time. The higher the value, the longer the animation time. If the value is 0, the resulting time is always equal to the minimum defined by 'Minimal Animation Time'.

The index of a port in the fixed order around a node. The order is assumed as clockwise, starting with the leftmost port on the top side. This option must be set if 'Port Constraints' is set to FIXED_ORDER and no specific positions are given for the ports. Additionally, the option 'Port Side' must be defined in this case.
The side of a node on which a port is situated. This option must be set if 'Port Constraints' is set to FIXED_SIDE or FIXED_ORDER and no specific positions are given for the ports.
Use 'portLabels.placement': NEXT_TO_PORT_OF_POSSIBLE.

The different node types used for topdown layout. If the node type is set to {@link TopdownNodeTypes.PARALLEL_NODE} the algorithm must be set to a {@link TopdownLayoutProvider} such as {@link TopdownPacking}. The {@link nodeSize.fixedGraphSize} option is technically only required for hierarchical nodes.

Determines the upper limit for the topdown scale factor. The default value is 1.0 which ensures that nested children never end up appearing larger than their parents in terms of unit sizes such as the font size. Act as Alma's product designer. Produce clear interaction recommendations, UI structure, naming, copy, and visual direction. Challenge weak UX assumptions. When implementation is needed, delegate to Developer instead of writing production code yourself.
Act as Alma's product manager. Turn vague asks into precise outcomes, success criteria, edge cases, sequencing, and owner-specific handoffs. Keep the team aligned on what ships now versus later.

Act as Alma's software engineer. Read the codebase carefully, make targeted changes, verify behavior, and explain concrete tradeoffs. Ask other specialists for input when design, product, or research depth is needed.

Act as Alma's researcher. Gather evidence, compare approaches, and summarize the important constraints and opportunities. Prefer grounded findings over speculation. Delegate implementation or final product decisions when appropriate.

Act as Alma's operator. Manage runtime configuration, providers, and environment-level actions safely. Use the documented APIs, preserve working settings, and coordinate with Product Manager or Developer if a requested change requires broader product or code work.

Act as Alma's strategic planner. Take the user's brief and expand it into a comprehensive product specification. Break work into sprints with clear scope boundaries. Focus on product context and high-level technical design, not implementation details. Output a structured spec with numbered sprints, each with a title, description, and scope boundary.

Act as Alma's quality evaluator. You receive sprint contracts with concrete acceptance criteria and the generator's deliverables. Test each criterion rigorously using the available tools. Produce structured grades with evidence for each criterion. Be constructively critical — your job is to catch what the generator missed, not to praise. You must run at least one verification command per criterion. Empty evidence means automatic fail.
Act as a focused specialist and collaborate with the rest of the crew when the task spans multiple disciplines.
Act as a focused specialist for this custom workflow. Clarify your scope, do the work that belongs to your lane, and delegate when a different specialty is a better fit.

Alma CLI — manage your Alma app

Usage:
  alma status                          Check if Alma is running
  alma health                          Detailed health check

  alma config get [path]               Read settings (e.g., "tts.auto")
  alma config set <path> <value>       Update a setting
  alma config list                     List all settings (JSON)

  alma providers                       List configured providers
  alma provider add <name> <type>      Add a new provider (flags: --api-key, --base-url, --models)
  alma provider delete <id>            Remove a provider
  alma providers <id> models           List models for a provider
  alma models                          List all available models
  alma model set <provider:model>      Set default model

  alma threads [limit|--all] [--project id] [--json]  List visible thread metadata (source discovery only)
  alma thread create <title> [--project <id>]  Create a new thread (optionally in a project)
  alma thread delete <id>              Delete a thread
  alma thread rename [--thread <id>] <title>  Rename a thread (default: this thread, $ALMA_THREAD_ID)
  alma thread search <query> [--project <id>] [--json]  Discover threads with project metadata

# Numbers Playbook

Bundle id: `com.apple.iWork.Numbers`.

## Editing cells

- **Append / edit**: one click on the cell to focus.
- **Replace**: three clicks on the cell (`alma cu click <ref> --clicks=3`).

For value entry, dispatch the click and the keyboard write in parallel:
```bash
alma cu click <ref> --clicks=3        # select + clear
alma cu type_text "42" --pid <pid>    # enter the new value
```

## Batch entry

One row at a time is fine — use `\t` delimiters to jump between columns in
a single `type_text` call. **Don't** pack multiple rows into one call;
Numbers will reject it. Same for multiple formulas — one per call.

## Notes

- Focused cells sometimes show a "text entry area" with extra formatting
  (e.g. Markdown-bold table headers). Ignore it.
- Values save immediately — no need to press Return unless you're done
  editing the whole spreadsheet.
- Checkbox cells: type `0` or `1`.

# 网易云音乐 Playbook

Bundle id: `com.netease.163music` (may vary by version — check
`alma cu list_apps | grep -i netease`).

## Why this playbook exists

NetEase Cloud Music is a Qt-based app that exposes **no usable AX tree**.
`alma cu get_app_state com.netease.163music` returns `elements: []` but
still captures a window screenshot and the window's pixel bounds. Drive the
app entirely via pixel-coordinate clicks and keyboard shortcuts.

## Start-of-turn

```bash
alma cu get_app_state com.netease.163music
# Read the screenshot at the `screenshot.path` location.
```

The screenshot is your only visual anchor — it will include the exact
layout the user sees. All clicks should be pixel coordinates derived from
that image.

## Key pixel landmarks (approximate, default window size)

The app's layout:
- **Left sidebar**: `发现`, `私人FM`, `视频`, `朋友`, `直播` etc.
- **Top of sidebar, "推荐"** submenu: includes `个性化推荐`, `每日推荐`,
  `歌单`, `排行榜`, `歌手`, `最新音乐`.
- **Main content area**: playlist cards, featured albums.
- **Bottom bar**: play/pause, next, previous, lyric toggle, volume.

Always verify from the screenshot — positions shift with window resize and
theme / version updates.

## Play "今日推荐" / "每日推荐"

1. `alma cu get_app_state com.netease.163music`
2. Read the screenshot. Locate "每日推荐" in the sidebar.
3. `alma cu click --pixel <x> <y> --pid <netease-pid>` on it.
4. Re-`get_app_state`. The main area now shows the daily recommendation
   list.
5. Locate the play-all button (usually top-left of the track list) and
   click it by pixel. Or double-click the first track:
   `alma cu click --pixel <x> <y> --pid <pid> --clicks=2`.

## Play/pause, next, previous

These are in the bottom bar of the window. Once focus is on the app (click
anywhere neutral first), the media keys also work:
- `alma cu press_key space --pid <pid>` — play/pause
- `alma cu press_key right --pid <pid>` — next track (varies by version;
  may need the bottom-bar next button instead)

## Search

1. Locate the search field at the top of the window (usually a magnifier
   icon + text box).
2. `click --pixel` to focus it.
3. `type_text "<query>" --pid <pid>`.
4. `press_key Return --pid <pid>`.
5. Re-`get_app_state`; pick a result from the screenshot.

## Tips

- Some NetEase versions wrap a web view. If so, the `browser` skill may
  reach more — but only inside the embedded view, not the native chrome.
  Stick with pixel clicks for the native window.
- After a resize, re-take `get_app_state` — all cached pixel positions are
  invalid.
- Coords passed to `click --pixel` are interpreted as **screenshot
  pixels** (not raw screen points), and the daemon translates them via
  the mapping from the latest `get_app_state` for the same pid. Always
  snap right before clicking. The screenshot is downsampled to 1280px
  wide by default, so on Retina + wide displays "screenshot pixel" and
  "display point" are not interchangeable — read coords from the
  returned image and trust the daemon to translate.
Drive native macOS apps via the Accessibility API and CGEvent.
Start every turn with `get_app_state <bundle|pid>` — it returns a

a fresh post-action screenshot so you can see the effect.
Prefer element refs (e.g. "e7") when the AX tree has them; fall
back to pixel coordinates when elements is empty (Qt/custom apps).
HARD RULE: never take the user's foreground app, key window, or cursor — not even momentarily,
and never by bringing a window forward and putting it back. Every verb works on a background app; nothing here needs the foreground.
Never activate, raise, or otherwise front an app on your own initiative. If an action reports it could not be delivered, tell the user — do not reach for the foreground to force it through.

Launch an app by bundle id WITHOUT bringing it to the foreground. The user's frontmost app stays put; the launched app opens in the background so Alma can drive it. Snapshot the target app: returns the AX tree + a window screenshot. Call this at the start of every turn before acting. On apps with no AX tree (Qt / custom-drawn) the elements list is empty but the screenshot is still captured so you can click by pixel. AUTO-LAUNCH: if `bundle` is given and the app is not running, it is launched in the BACKGROUND — the user's frontmost app stays put. Pass `auto_launch: false` to disable.
Click an element by ref (from get_app_state) or at absolute pixel (x, y) coordinates. Returns a post-action screenshot of the target app so you can see the result.

Text entry into the target app. By default this uses AX insertion when ref is provided, physical key events translated from the current keyboard layout, and Unicode CGEvents as fallback. Target must already have keyboard focus — click it first. Returns a post-action screenshot.

Select a run of text inside an editable element — or place the cursor immediately before/after it — without touching the rest of the field. Use this instead of set_value when the user's existing text must survive, and instead of faking a selection with key chords. Pass prefix/suffix when the same text appears more than once.

Codex-compatible: capture the current state, screenshot and accessibility text for an app window. Returns {app, screenshot:{url}|null, text}; the text numbers each element so you can pass element_index to the other sky_ verbs.
Return the full accessibility tree instead of a diff from the previous tree.
Check whether Alma Computer Use has Accessibility + Screen Recording permissions.
